newsitem.title: CHINA: Occidental, Texaco to seek oil off China.
newsitem.headline: Occidental, Texaco to seek oil off China.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp and Texaco Inc of the United States have signed a contract with China to explore for oil in the Bohai Bay, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

Under the contract signed with the China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) on Tuesday, Occidental and Texaco will explore 2,340 sq km of the western part of the Bohai Bay, the newspaper said, quoting CNOOC officials. The average water depth in the area is 10-20 metres, it said.

The contract calls for Occidental and Texaco to shoulder all exploration risks. Occidental and Texaco will have a 50-50 interest in the exploration with Texaco acting as the operator, the newspaper said.
A previous agreement between CNOOC and Occidental had allowed the U.S. company to conduct seismological research for a year.
The newspaper said an increasing number of foreign oil firms have been attracted to the Bohai Bay due to a rising number of new finds.
Currently, 11 joint venture contracts between CNOOC and foreign companies are in operation in the area.
Officials predict there will be at least 10 new wells in the bay next year, the newspaper said.
Four of the operational fields in the bay are expected to produce a total of 2.0 million tonnes of oil and 400 million cubic metres of natural gas this year, it said.
In 1997, seven more oil fields will be developed in the Bohai Bay, the daily said.
